examples.en: A donation box is placed in front of the station.
The students put a little of their allowance into the donation box.
They held a donation box and asked for help on the street.

examples.ko: 카페 계산대 옆에 작은 모금함이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small donation box next to the cafe counter.

examples.ko: 모금함은 한 달에 한 번 열어서 확인해요.
examples.en: We open the donation box once a month to check it.
The donation box was full too, so we had to empty it.

explain: 연말에 구세군 냄비나 편의점, 학교에서 보는 것처럼 기부금을 넣는 통을 말해요. '모금함에 넣다', '모금함을 설치하다'처럼 써요. 사람들에게 돈을 모으는 일 자체는 '모금'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a box where you drop donations, like the ones seen at year-end charity drives, stores and schools. It is used as '모금함에 넣다' or '모금함을 설치하다'. The act of collecting money itself is called '모금'.

examples.ko: 미납금이 있으면 서비스를 이용할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't use the service if you have an unpaid balance.

examples.ko: 이번 달 안에 미납금을 내 주세요.
examples.en: Please pay the outstanding balance within this month.
I got a text message about an unpaid bill.

examples.ko: 관리비 미납금은 벌써 세 달 치예요.
examples.en: The unpaid maintenance fees already add up to three months.
Late fees are added to unpaid amounts.

examples.ko: 미납금을 한꺼번에 내기 어려우면 나눠서 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If it's hard to pay the overdue amount all at once, you can pay in installments.

explain: 요금, 세금, 관리비처럼 내야 하는데 아직 내지 않은 돈이에요. 고지서나 안내 문자에서 자주 보고, '미납금을 납부하다', '연체료'와 같이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '밀린 돈'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to money such as fees, taxes or maintenance charges that should have been paid but hasn't. You see it on bills and notice messages, often alongside '미납금을 납부하다' (pay the overdue amount) and '연체료' (late fee). In casual talk people also say '밀린 돈' (money in arrears).

examples.en: I went to my friend's wedding and gave a monetary gift.
I don't know how much to give as a monetary gift.
I sent condolence money to my friend's father's funeral.

examples.ko: 부조금 봉투에 이름을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must write your name on the money envelope.
At work, we collected money from the staff separately as a gift.

examples.ko: 부조금은 축하나 위로하는 마음을 담아 내요.
examples.en: People give this money to express congratulations or comfort.

explain: 결혼식이나 장례식처럼 큰일이 있는 집에 돕는 마음으로 내는 돈이에요. 결혼식에는 '축의금', 장례식에는 '조의금'이라고 나누어 말하기도 해요. 보통 봉투에 넣어서 내요.
explain_en: It is money given to a family holding a big event, such as a wedding or funeral, as a way of helping out. People often distinguish '축의금' for weddings and '조의금' for funerals. It is usually handed over in an envelope.

examples.en: Yesterday I sent my parents some money.
You can send money easily with the app.
I send money right after I get paid.
There's a fee to send money overseas.
If you give me your account number, I'll send the money right away.
I sent money to the wrong person by mistake.

explain: 은행 계좌에서 다른 계좌로 돈을 보내는 것을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '이체하다'도 쓰는데, '이체'는 은행 서비스 이름처럼 자주 보이고 '송금'은 상대에게 보낸다는 느낌이 강해요. 현금을 직접 주는 건 '주다', 택배로 보내는 건 '부치다'예요.
explain_en: It means sending money from your bank account to someone else's. 이체하다 is a close synonym that you see more in banking menus, while 송금하다 stresses sending to a person. Handing over cash is 주다, and mailing something is 부치다.

examples.en: At the end of every month, I go around to clients and collect unpaid bills.

examples.ko: 지방에 푼 물건값을 수금하려고 출장을 갔어요.
examples.en: I went on a business trip to collect payment for goods sent out to the provinces.
The secretary took on the job of collecting dues.

examples.ko: 이번 달 요금은 다음 주에 수금할 예정이에요.
examples.en: We plan to collect this month's charges next week.

examples.ko: 직원이 가게를 찾아와 월세를 수금해 갔어요.
examples.en: A staff member came to the shop and collected the monthly rent.
It isn't easy to collect old unpaid bills.

explain: 돈을 받는 쪽에서 '받을 돈을 받아 모으다'라는 뜻으로 써요. 회비를 걷는 정도의 일상적인 일은 보통 '걷다'를 써서 '회비를 걷다'라고 말해요. 돈을 내는 쪽은 '내다', '납부하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is said from the receiving side, meaning to gather money that is owed to you. For everyday things like collecting dues, people usually use '걷다' instead, as in '회비를 걷다'. The paying side uses '내다' or '납부하다'.

examples.en: There is a test drive of the new car this afternoon.

examples.ko: 시승을 해 보고 나서 차를 사기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to buy the car after taking a test drive.

examples.ko: 시승은 예약한 사람만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who made a reservation can take a test drive.
The reporters who took part in the test drive left their reviews.
The test drive reviews were good, so I went with high expectations.

examples.ko: 이번 시승 차량은 새로 나온 전기차예요.
examples.en: This test-drive car is the newly released electric car.

explain: 사려고 하거나 새로 나온 차를 직접 타 보는 것을 말해요. '시승을 하다', '시승 행사', '시승 후기'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '시운전'은 만들거나 고친 차를 시험 삼아 운전해 보는 것이라 차이가 있어요.
explain_en: It means actually riding or driving a car you are thinking of buying or a newly released car. It appears in '시승을 하다', '시승 행사' and '시승 후기'. The similar '시운전' is about trial-running a car that was just built or repaired, so it differs.

examples.ko: 서류를 우송하는 데 보통 이삼 일이 걸려서 일정에 여유를 두었어요.
examples.en: Mailing documents usually takes two or three days, so I left some leeway in the schedule.
I'll mail the contract to your address tomorrow.

examples.ko: 책을 우송하려면 먼저 포장부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: To mail the book, you need to wrap it first.

examples.ko: 합격 증서를 집으로 우송했다고 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got word that they mailed the certificate of acceptance to my home.
I received the documents you mailed today.
I'll mail the item this afternoon.

explain: 우편으로 보낸다는 점이 분명한 딱딱한 말이라 공문이나 안내문에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '부치다'나 '보내다'를 쓰고, 택배로 보낼 때는 '택배로 보내다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal word that makes clear something goes by post, so it appears in official notices. In daily life people say '부치다' or '보내다', and for courier delivery '택배로 보내다'.

examples.en: I pay rent by automatic transfer.
How much is the transfer fee?

examples.ko: 이체가 아직 안 된 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the transfer hasn't gone through yet.
Making a transfer with the app is convenient.
I went over today's transfer limit.

examples.ko: 이체 내역은 앱에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see your transfer history in the app.

explain: '이체'는 은행 계좌에서 다른 계좌로 돈을 보내는 것이에요. 말할 때는 보통 '송금'이나 '입금'을 더 많이 쓰고, '이체'는 은행 앱이나 '자동 이체'처럼 은행 용어로 자주 보여요. 다른 사람에게 돈을 보내면 송금, 받는 쪽에서 돈이 들어오면 입금이에요.
explain_en: 이체 means moving money from one bank account to another. In conversation people more often say 송금 or 입금, while 이체 shows up in bank apps and in 자동 이체. Sending money to someone is 송금, and money arriving on the receiving side is 입금.

examples.en: I transferred money to my friend.
I will transfer the salary into the account tomorrow.
If you transfer with the app, there is no fee.

examples.ko: 이체하기 전에 계좌 번호를 한 번 더 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the account number once more before transferring.

examples.ko: 방금 보험료를 이체해서 확인 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I just transferred the insurance payment and got a confirmation text.
Where should I transfer it?

explain: '이체하다'는 계좌에서 계좌로 돈을 옮기는 것이에요. 은행 앱에는 '이체하기' 버튼이 많고, 말할 때는 '송금하다'나 '보내다'도 자주 써요. 돈을 받는 곳은 현금이 아니라 '계좌'예요.
explain_en: 이체하다 means moving money from one account to another. Bank apps often have a button labeled 이체하기, and in speech people also say 송금하다 or 보내다. The money goes to an account, not to cash in hand.

en: look up; check (records); make an inquiry

examples.en: I check my account balance in the app.

examples.ko: 주문 내역을 조회해서 배송 상태를 확인했어요.
examples.en: I looked up my order history and checked the delivery status.

examples.ko: 번호를 입력하면 정보를 조회할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you enter the number, you can look up the information.

examples.ko: 조회하는 데 시간이 오래 걸려서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The lookup took a long time, so I waited.
I checked my grades on the school website.
Even if you do not check yourself, it comes as a notification.

explain: 은행, 인터넷, 관공서에서 이미 있는 기록을 찾아볼 때 써요. '검색하다'는 넓은 인터넷에서 찾는 것이고, '조회하다'는 내 정보나 정해진 자료를 확인하는 느낌이에요. '잔액 조회', '주문 조회'처럼 메뉴 이름으로 많이 봐요.
explain_en: Used for looking up existing records at banks, websites, and public offices. '검색하다' is searching the wide internet, while 조회하다 is checking your own data or a fixed set of records. It often appears as menu names like '잔액 조회' and '주문 조회'.

examples.en: Please write your name and address on the order form.
I checked the order form and packed the goods.
The order form came in wrong, so I sent it back.
We accept group order forms by email.

examples.ko: 주문서를 보내 주시면 배송을 확인해 드려요.
examples.en: If you send me the order form, I'll check the delivery for you.

examples.ko: 식당 직원이 주문서를 들고 주방으로 갔어요.
examples.en: The restaurant staff took the order slip to the kitchen.

explain: '주문'은 시키는 행동이고, '주문서'는 그 내용을 적은 종이나 양식이에요. 돈을 낸 증거인 '영수증'과는 달라요.
explain_en: '주문' is the act of ordering, while '주문서' is the paper or form that lists what was ordered. It differs from a '영수증' (receipt), which proves payment.

examples.ko: 진열대 가격표를 보고 손님들 눈이 휘둥그레졌어요.
examples.en: The customers' eyes grew wide when they saw the price tags on the display stand.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 과자가 진열대 맨 앞에 있어요.
examples.en: The newly released snack is at the very front of the display stand.
I filled the display stand with goods neatly.
A child is running around between the shelves in the mart.

examples.ko: 인기 상품은 금방 팔려서 진열대가 비었어요.
examples.en: The popular items sold out quickly, so the display stand is empty.

examples.ko: 이 진열대는 높아서 손이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: This display stand is so high that I can't reach it.

explain: 가게에서 물건을 올려 두고 보여 주는 선반이에요. 유리로 닫힌 '진열장'과 달리 열려 있어서 손님이 바로 집을 수 있는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a shelf in a shop where goods are placed to show them. Unlike a glass-enclosed '진열장', it is open, giving the feeling that customers can pick things up directly.

examples.ko: 어제 주문하신 상품은 오늘 출고할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The item you ordered yesterday is scheduled to ship out today.

examples.ko: 공장에서는 제품을 출고하기 전에 검사를 한 번 더 해요.
examples.en: At the factory, they inspect products once more before shipping them out.

examples.ko: 주문이 많아서 하루에 천 개씩 출고해요.
examples.en: There are many orders, so we ship out a thousand a day.
We're out of stock, so we can't ship it right now.

examples.ko: 자동차 회사가 신형 모델을 다음 달에 출고한대요.
examples.en: I heard the car company will release the new model next month.

examples.ko: 창고에서 출고하는 데 보통 이틀쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It usually takes about two days to ship out from the warehouse.

explain: 공장이나 창고에서 물건을 내보낼 때 쓰고, 반대말은 '입고'예요. 쇼핑몰의 '출고 완료' 알림이나 새 차를 받는 '신차 출고'처럼 생활에서도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used when goods leave a factory or warehouse, and the opposite is '입고' (goods coming in). You often see it in shopping apps as '출고 완료' (shipped) and in '신차 출고' (taking delivery of a new car).

examples.en: I needed cash, so I withdrew money from the ATM.

examples.ko: 통장에서 한 번에 얼마까지 출금할 수 있어요?
examples.en: How much can I withdraw from the account at once?
You can withdraw even without a card, using a phone.
A fee is added when withdrawing.
As soon as my salary comes in, the rent is automatically withdrawn.
How do I get back money that was withdrawn by mistake?

explain: '출금하다'는 은행 계좌에서 돈을 빼는 일이고, 반대로 넣는 건 '입금하다'예요. 현금을 찾을 때는 '돈을 찾다'가 말로 더 자연스러워요. 자동으로 빠져나갈 때는 '출금되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 출금하다 means taking money out of a bank account, and putting money in is 입금하다. In speech, 돈을 찾다 sounds more natural for getting cash. When money is taken automatically, use 출금되다.

dis.h: money going out of an account, banking term

p.n: 인출하다 stresses drawing the cash out; 출금하다 stresses the money leaving the account.
